mainTopic: ניקנור's miraculous doors, and the families who kept their Temple skills secret: בית גרמו and בית אבטינס
overview: This amud opens with the last word of the earlier discussion about הלני המלכה's tablet. It then tells the story of the miracles of ניקנור's doors and explains why the שערי ניקנור were the only gates of the מקדש not changed to gold. Next, the משנה lists people remembered for disgrace: בית גרמו, בית אבטינס, הוגרס בן לוי and בן קמצר, who all refused to teach their special skills. It closes both lists with the פסוק ״זכר צדיק לברכה ושם רשעים ירקב״. The גמרא tells how the חכמים tried to replace בית גרמו (the לחם הפנים) and בית אבטינס (the קטורת) with craftsmen from Alexandria. The replacements failed, and the families came back only for double pay. Both families explain that they kept their secrets so the skills could never serve עבודה זרה after the חורבן. They are praised for staying above suspicion, ״והייתם נקיים מה׳ ומישראל״. Three stories about descendants of בית אבטינס follow, ending with רבי עקיבא ruling that one may no longer speak badly of them. בן עזאי then begins a lesson, continued on the next amud: what is truly yours will come back to you.

steps.title: The Tablet Was Written in Alternating Form
steps.stepSummary: The previous discussion closes. הלני המלכה's tablet was written בסירוגין, so it proves nothing about writing a מגילה for a תינוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was written in alternating form: some full words, some only first letters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes pushing away a proof from the earlier discussion. The answer is that הלני המלכה's tablet was written בסירוגין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא had tried to prove that you may write a short scroll of פסוקים for a child to learn from, using הלני's tablet of the פרשת סוטה. The answer is that the tablet did not contain the full text. It had opening words, and the rest of each פסוק appeared only as initials. Since it was not a real written section of the תורה, it cannot be a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: In alternating form: some words written fully, others only as initials

steps.confusionAlert: This single word belongs to the PREVIOUS discussion about הלני המלכה's tablet. It has nothing to do with the ניקנור story that comes next.

phrases.english: In alternating form.
phrases.notes: The tablet had some full words and some initials only, so it was not a true written passage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion about הלני המלכה's tablet, which began on the previous amud.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using הלני's tablet as proof that a partial scroll may be written for a child.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The tablet did not contain full text. It used initials for most words, so it is not comparable to a written scroll.

steps.title: The משנה: Miracles Happened to ניקנור's Doors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which says miracles happened to ניקנור's doors.
steps.simpleTranslation: For ניקנור, miracles were done to his doors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new topic by quoting the next line from the משנה. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists people who were praised for their contributions to the מקדש. About ניקנור, it only says that miracles happened to his doors. It does not say what the miracles were, so the גמרא will need to fill that in.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who brought copper doors from Egypt for the eastern gate of the מקדש

phrases.english: Nicanor: miracles were performed for his doors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. Moves from הלני המלכה to ניקנור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Miracles happened to ניקנור's doors, which is why he is remembered for praise.

steps.title: What Were the Miracles?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks what miracles the משנה is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: What miracles happened to his doors?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a simple question: which miracles is the משנה referring to? This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge. It is a request for details the משנה left out. The answer will be a full story.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught: introduces a ברייתא

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
What miracles were performed for his doors?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מָה נִסִּים נַעֲשׂוּ לְדַלְתוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the משנה just quoted.

steps.title: The Storm and the First Door Thrown Overboard
steps.stepSummary: On the way back from אלכסנדריא, a storm threatened the ship. The sailors threw one door into the sea, but the storm did not stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: When ניקנור went to bring doors from אלכסנדריא in Egypt, a storm wave rose against him on the way back and threatened to drown him. They took one of the doors and threw it into the sea, but the sea still did not calm down.
steps.whatsHappening: The story begins. A storm hits the ship, and the passengers throw one heavy door overboard to lighten the load.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doors were very heavy copper, so getting rid of one seemed like a sensible way to save the ship. The detail that the sea did not calm afterward sets up the miracle that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: אלכסנדריא, the city in Egypt where the doors were made

phrases.english: They said: When Nicanor went
to bring doors from Alexandria of Egypt,

phrases.aramaic: בַּחֲזִירָתוֹ עָמַד עָלָיו נַחְשׁוֹל שֶׁבַּיָּם לְטַבְּעוֹ,
phrases.english: on his return, a storm of the sea rose against him to drown him,
they took one of them and threw it into the sea,
and still the sea did not rest from its rage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question by telling the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The miracle story begins with a storm on the voyage home.

steps.title: ניקנור Embraces the Second Door
steps.stepSummary: When the sailors tried to throw in the second door, ניקנור hugged it and said to throw him in with it. The sea calmed immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: They wanted to throw the second door in. He stood and wrapped himself around it and said: Throw me in with it. Right away the sea calmed. But he was sad about the other door.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first miracle. ניקנור is ready to give his life rather than lose the second door, and the storm stops at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ניקנור's devotion to the מקדש is the turning point of the story. The sea calms without anyone being thrown in, so the second door is saved. He still grieves over the first door, which sets up the next miracle.

phrases.english: They sought to throw its companion,
he stood and embraced it,
he said to them: Throw me in with it.
Immediately the sea rested from its rage,
and he was grieving over its companion.
phrases.notes: He was sad about the first door, which had been lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with the first miracle.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First miracle: the sea calmed because of ניקנור's self-sacrifice.

steps.title: The Lost Door Reappears at עכו
steps.stepSummary: When they reached the port of עכו, the lost door surfaced from under the ship. Another version says a sea creature swallowed it and spat it onto land.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he reached the port of עכו, the door was poking out from under the sides of the ship. Some say a sea creature swallowed it and spat it out onto dry land.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second miracle. The copper door that was thrown into the sea comes back. Two versions are given of how it happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A heavy copper door should have sunk to the bottom, yet it traveled with the ship and appeared at the port. The יש אומרים version tells a different way the door returned, but both agree that it came back by a miracle.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: introduces another version

phrases.english: When he arrived at the port of Akko,
it was poking out and emerging
from under the sides of the ship.
And some say a sea creature swallowed it,
and spat it out onto dry land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story with the second miracle and gives an alternate version.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Second miracle: the lost door miraculously came back.

steps.title: שלמה's Verse: A Covenant with the Sea
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא connects the story to a פסוק by שלמה, reading ברותים as ברית ים.
steps.simpleTranslation: About this שלמה said: 'The beams of our houses are cedars, our doors are cypresses (ברותים).' Do not read it as ברותים, but as ברית ים, a covenant of the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows that the miracle is hinted at in a פסוק from שיר השירים, using a wordplay דרשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about doors, and by rereading ברותים as ברית ים, the doors are described as having a covenant with the sea. This gives the story a basis in the פסוק: the sea was bound to bring the door back to its place.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as: a wordplay דרשה

phrases.english: And about this Solomon said:
"The beams of our houses are cedars,
our doors are cypresses",
do not read "cypresses (berotim)",
but rather "covenant of the sea (berit yam)".

steps.confusionAlert: אל תיקרי does not change the actual text of the פסוק. It adds an extra layer of meaning on top of the plain reading.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a scriptural anchor for the story just told.
steps.raayaObject: The miracle of the door returning from the sea.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שיר השירים 1:17, read with a דרשה as ברית ים.

steps.title: All Gates Turned to Gold Except ניקנור's
steps.stepSummary: Because of the miracles, the שערי ניקנור were left as they were when all the other gates of the מקדש were changed to gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, all the gates in the מקדש were changed to be gold, except the gates of ניקנור, because miracles were done with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא draws a practical result from the story. The miracle doors were kept as they were and not replaced with gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Later, when the people became wealthy, they upgraded every gate to gold. The שערי ניקנור were the one exception, because the miracle made the original doors special and worth keeping. This is the first of several reasons given for the exception.

keyTerms.meaning: The gates of ניקנור, the eastern gates of the עזרה

phrases.english: Therefore, all the gates that were in the Temple
were changed to be of gold,
except for the gates of Nicanor
because miracles were performed with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical result from the miracle story.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a miracle can give an object lasting honor that is preserved instead of being upgraded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שערי ניקנור alone were not changed to gold, because of the miracles.

steps.title: Another Reason: Their Copper Was Brightly Colored
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion says the doors were not replaced because their copper was a bright golden color.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it was because their copper was golden-colored.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא offers a different reason why the שערי ניקנור were not replaced with gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, the reason was not the miracle but how the doors looked. The copper was so bright that it already resembled gold, so there was no need to replace it.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנְּחוֹשְׁתָּן מוּצְהֶבֶת הָיְתָה.
phrases.english: And some say: because their copper was golden-colored.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנְּחוֹשְׁתָּן מוּצְהֶבֶת הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation for the same exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doors stayed because their copper already looked golden.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: Refined Copper That Shone Like Gold
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the copper was a refined kind that shone like gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: It was refined copper, and it shone like gold.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion, from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, describes the copper as a special refined kind that glowed like gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view is close to the יש אומרים, since both point to the quality of the copper. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds that it was a specific refined type, קלוניתא, bright enough to light up its surroundings like gold. Either way, replacing it with gold was unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who gives the third explanation

steps.whatToRemember: The שערי ניקנור were the only gates of the מקדש not changed to gold. There are three reasons: (1) miracles happened to them; (2) their copper was golden-colored; (3) according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, it was refined copper that shone like gold.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
it was refined copper,
and it shone like gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third explanation, similar to the second, that names a special refined copper.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doors were refined copper that shone like gold, so they did not need to be replaced.

steps.title: The משנה lists families remembered for disgrace
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts a new list of people remembered badly: בית גרמו would not teach how to make לחם הפנים, and בית אבטינס would not teach how to make the קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: And these are remembered for disgrace: בית גרמו did not want to teach how the לחם הפנים was made, and בית אבטינס did not want to teach how the קטורת was made.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now turns from the people remembered for praise to the people remembered for disgrace. The first two are families who kept their Temple skills secret.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה praised people like ניקנור who gave something to the מקדש. Here the opposite is shown. These families did their jobs well, but they refused to pass the skill on to others.

keyTerms.meaning: For disgrace; remembered in a bad way
The family in charge of baking the לחם הפנים
The shewbread placed on the שולחן in the מקדש each week
The family in charge of preparing the קטורת
The incense offered in the מקדש

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these are for disgrace:
Those of the House of Garmu

phrases.aramaic: לֹא רָצוּ לְלַמֵּד עַל מַעֲשֵׂה לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים,
phrases.english: did not want to teach about making the shewbread;
those of the House of Avtinas

phrases.aramaic: לֹא רָצוּ לְלַמֵּד עַל מַעֲשֵׂה הַקְּטוֹרֶת.
phrases.english: did not want to teach about making the incense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the people remembered for praise, such as ניקנור's gates, to the opposite group, those remembered for disgrace.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית גרמו and בית אבטינס are remembered badly because they refused to teach their Temple skills.

steps.title: Two more individuals who kept their skills secret
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds הוגרס בן לוי, who knew a special singing technique, and בן קמצר, who had a special writing skill. Neither would teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: הוגרס בן לוי knew a chapter in the art of song and did not want to teach it. בן קמצר did not want to teach his special way of writing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list with two individuals who also refused to share their skills.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list grows from families to single people. These are not only about baking and incense but also about the singing in the מקדש and the skill of writing. The fault is the same each time: keeping a skill for oneself.

keyTerms.meaning: A לוי who knew a special singing technique
A section or technique of song
A scribe with a special writing skill
The act or technique of writing

phrases.aramaic: הוּגְרַס בֶּן לֵוִי הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ פֶּרֶק בַּשִּׁיר
phrases.english: Hugras ben Levi knew a chapter in song
and did not want to teach it;
Ben Kamtzar did not want to teach
about the act of writing.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּגְרַס בֶּן לֵוִי הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ פֶּרֶק בַּשִּׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of people remembered for disgrace.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הוגרס בן לוי and בן קמצר are also remembered badly for not teaching their skills.

steps.title: A verse contrasting the righteous and the wicked
steps.stepSummary: The משנה closes with a פסוק from משלי. The memory of the praised people is a blessing, but the name of those who hid their skills will rot.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the first group it is said: 'The memory of the righteous shall be for a blessing.' And about these it is said: 'But the name of the wicked shall rot.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה wraps up both lists with one פסוק. The first half of the פסוק fits the praised people, and the second half fits the people who kept their skills secret.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "הראשונים" means the people praised earlier in the משנה. "אלו" means the four just listed. The two halves of a single פסוק in משלי give the final judgment on each group.

keyTerms.meaning: The first ones; here, the people praised earlier
The memory of the righteous is a blessing (משלי י:ז)
And the name of the wicked will rot

steps.whatToRemember: Those who gave to the מקדש, such as ניקנור, are remembered with זכר צדיק לברכה. Those who kept their Temple skills to themselves are remembered with ושם רשעים ירקב.

phrases.english: About the first ones it is said:
'The memory of the righteous shall be for a blessing,'
and about these it is said:
'But the name of the wicked shall rot.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final judgment on both the praised list and the disgraced list.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The praised people are blessed in memory. Those who hid their Temple skills are remembered badly.

steps.title: The חכמים replace בית גרמו with Alexandrian bakers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that בית גרמו were experts in baking לחם הפנים but refused to teach. So the חכמים brought in craftsmen from Alexandria in Egypt.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: תנו רבנן: בית גרמו were experts in making the לחם הפנים and did not want to teach. The חכמים sent for and brought craftsmen from Alexandria in Egypt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a ברייתא that tells the full story behind the משנה's line about בית גרמו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said that בית גרמו refused to teach. The ברייתא adds what happened next: the חכמים tried to replace them with outside experts.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this introduces a ברייתא
Alexandria, a large city in Egypt

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית גַּרְמוּ הָיוּ בְּקִיאִין בְּמַעֲשֵׂה לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים
phrases.english: The House of Garmu were experts in making the shewbread
and did not want to teach.
The Sages sent and brought craftsmen
from Alexandria of Egypt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בֵּית גַּרְמוּ הָיוּ בְּקִיאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the משנה's short mention of בית גרמו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים tried to replace בית גרמו with craftsmen from Alexandria.

steps.title: The new bakers could not match בית גרמו
steps.stepSummary: The Alexandrians could bake the bread but could not take it out of the oven the same way. They heated and baked from outside, while בית גרמו did it inside. As a result, the Alexandrians' bread went moldy, and בית גרמו's bread did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They knew how to bake like them but not how to remove the bread like them. These heated from outside and baked from outside, while those heated from inside and baked from inside. These ones' bread got moldy, and those ones' bread did not get moldy.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why the replacement plan failed: the new bakers' method was weaker, and the bread spoiled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לחם הפנים had to stay on the שולחן for a whole week, so it could not be allowed to spoil. Only בית גרמו's inside method kept it fresh. This shows their secret really was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: To remove bread from the oven
They heat or light the fire
These, used to point to one group versus the other

steps.confusionAlert: The word "הללו" (these) is used for both groups. The first "הללו" is the Alexandrians, who worked outside and whose bread went moldy. The second "הללו" is בית גרמו, who worked inside and whose bread stayed fresh.

phrases.english: And they knew how to bake like them,
but they did not know how to remove the bread like them.
For these heat from outside and bake from outside,
and those heat from inside and bake from inside.
These ones' bread becomes moldy,
and those ones' bread does not become moldy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the replacement bakers fell short.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only בית גרמו's method kept לחם הפנים from becoming moldy.

steps.title: The חכמים decide to bring back בית גרמו
steps.stepSummary: When the חכמים heard about the moldy bread, they said that everything הקדוש ברוך הוא created is for His honor, and they quoted a פסוק from ישעיה. So בית גרמו were to return to their position.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the חכמים heard of the matter, they said: Everything הקדוש ברוך הוא created, He created for His honor, as it says: 'Everyone called by My name, I created for My glory.' And בית גרמו returned to their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים change their decision. For the sake of the מקדש, they let בית גרמו come back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים reasoned that the honor of the מקדש matters more than their own dignity or their annoyance with בית גרמו. Since only בית גרמו could make the bread properly, כבוד שמים required bringing them back.

keyTerms.meaning: He created it for His honor
Everyone called by My name (ישעיה מג:ז)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a principle: for the honor of the מקדש, the חכמים were willing to give up their own position and rehire people they had dismissed.

phrases.english: When the Sages heard of the matter, they said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מַה שֶּׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Everything the Holy One, Blessed be He, created
He created for His honor,
as it says: 'Everyone called by My name,
I created for My glory.'
And the House of Garmu returned to their place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the failure described in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the honor of הקדוש ברוך הוא, בית גרמו were brought back.

steps.title: בית גרמו return only for double pay
steps.stepSummary: בית גרמו refused at first. They came back only when their wages were doubled, from 12 מנה a day to 24.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים sent for them, but they did not come. They doubled their wages, and they came. Every day they had taken twelve מנה, and today they take twenty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells what happened when the חכמים invited בית גרמו back: they agreed only for twice the pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here "היום" means 'now,' after they returned. This detail shows that the family used their secret to get more money, which adds to why the משנה remembers them badly.

keyTerms.meaning: A unit of money, equal to 100 זוז

phrases.english: The Sages sent for them, and they did not come;
they doubled their wages, and they came.

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיוּ נוֹטְלִין שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מָנֶה,
phrases.english: Every day they used to take twelve maneh,
and today, twenty-four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after the decision to bring them back.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית גרמו's wages were doubled from 12 to 24 מנה a day.

steps.title: רבי יהודה gives different wage numbers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says their daily wage was 24 מנה at first and became 48 after they returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Every day they took twenty-four, and today forty-eight.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different version of the wage amounts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that the wages were doubled. They disagree only on the starting number: 12 or 24. So in רבי יהודה's version, the final pay is 48 instead of 24.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who gives an alternative version

steps.whatToRemember: בית גרמו refused to teach, could not be replaced, and returned only for double pay. Everyone agrees the pay doubled. The only dispute is whether it went from 12 to 24 or from 24 to 48.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Every day, twenty-four,
and today, forty-eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּכׇל יוֹם עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the wage numbers from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the wages went from 24 to 48 מנה a day.

steps.title: The חכמים ask בית גרמו why they refused to teach
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask בית גרמו what reason they had for not teaching their baking skill to others.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said to them: What reason did you have for not teaching?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that בית גרמו are back at work, the חכמים ask them why they kept their skill secret. This question sets up their answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the story made בית גרמו look selfish, as if they only wanted more money. This question opens the door to a different picture. Maybe they had a good reason for keeping the secret.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? This means: what reason did you have?

phrases.english: The Sages said to them:
What did you see that made you not teach?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם חֲכָמִים: מָה רְאִיתֶם שֶׁלֹּא לְלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after בית גרמו returned. Now the חכמים ask for their motive.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason בית גרמו refused to teach their baking technique.

steps.title: בית גרמו explain: fear that the skill would be used for idol worship
steps.stepSummary: Their family knew the בית המקדש would be destroyed. They were afraid that an unworthy person would learn the skill and use it for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to them: Our father's family knew that this House, the בית המקדש, would one day be destroyed. They worried that an unworthy person might learn the skill and then go and use it for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: בית גרמו answer the question. They kept the secret for a holy reason, not a selfish one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the בית המקדש is gone, there is no holy place left to use this special baking skill. The only place it could still be used is in idol worship. Keeping the secret within the family protected a holy skill from being misused.

phrases.english: They said to them:
Those of our father's house knew
that this House is destined to be destroyed,
and they worried lest an unworthy person learn it
and go and serve idols with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם: יוֹדְעִין הָיוּ שֶׁל בֵּית אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They hid the skill so that, after the Temple's destruction, no unworthy person could use it for idol worship.

steps.title: בית גרמו are praised: their children never ate fine bread
steps.stepSummary: בית גרמו are remembered for good because their children never had fine white bread. This way no one could suspect them of feeding themselves from the לחם הפנים technique. They fulfilled the פסוק ״והייתם נקיים מה׳ ומישראל״.
steps.simpleTranslation: For this they are remembered with praise. Fine bread was never found in their children's hands, so that people would not say they were living off the work of the לחם הפנים. This fulfills the verse: "And you shall be clean before ה׳ and before Israel."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds praise for בית גרמו. They were careful that no one could ever suspect them of misusing their Temple skill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not enough to be innocent before ה׳. A person should also avoid anything that makes other people suspect him. By eating only plain bread, the family left no room for gossip.

keyTerms.meaning: Be clean before ה׳ and before Israel. This means: stay above suspicion (במדבר ל״ב:כ״ב).

steps.whyThisMatters: This פסוק is the classic source for the rule that a person must avoid even the appearance of wrongdoing, not only actual wrongdoing.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה מַזְכִּירִין אוֹתָן לְשֶׁבַח:
phrases.english: And for this matter they are mentioned with praise:

phrases.aramaic: מֵעוֹלָם לֹא נִמְצֵאת פַּת נְקִיָּה בְּיַד בְּנֵיהֶם,
phrases.english: fine bread was never found in the hands of their children,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ מִמַּעֲשֵׂה לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים זֶה נִיזּוֹנִין,
phrases.english: so that people would not say: they are fed from the making of the לחם הפנים,
to fulfill what is stated:
"And you shall be clean before ה׳ and before Israel."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה מַזְכִּירִין אוֹתָן לְשֶׁבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the בית גרמו story by turning them into a model of righteous behavior.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית גרמו stayed above suspicion by never eating fine bread. This fulfills ״והייתם נקיים״.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about בית אבטינס and the incense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: בית אבטינס refused to teach how to make the קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The family of בית אבטינס did not want to teach how the incense was made.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next family listed in the משנה. This quote sets up the ברייתא that tells their story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like בית גרמו, this family had a secret Temple skill. Theirs was the קטורת, the incense, instead of the bread. The two stories will run in parallel.

keyTerms.meaning: The family in charge of making the Temple incense
The incense offered in the בית המקדש

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל בֵּית אַבְטִינָס לֹא רָצוּ לְלַמֵּד
phrases.english: Those of the House of Avtinas did not want to teach
about the making of the incense.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁל בֵּית אַבְטִינָס לֹא רָצוּ לְלַמֵּד עַל מַעֲשֵׂה הַקְּטוֹרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from בית גרמו to the next family in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית אבטינס refused to teach the making of the קטורת.

steps.title: A ברייתא: Alexandrian craftsmen replace בית אבטינס
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says בית אבטינס were experts in the קטורת but refused to teach, so the חכמים brought craftsmen from Alexandria in Egypt.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: בית אבטינס were experts in making the קטורת, but they did not want to teach. So the חכמים sent for craftsmen from Alexandria in Egypt and brought them.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא begins the story of בית אבטינס. The חכמים replace them, just as they replaced בית גרמו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening is almost word for word the same as the בית גרמו story. Noticing the pattern helps the learner follow along. Only the skill is different.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית אַבְטִינָס הָיוּ בְּקִיאִין בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַקְּטוֹרֶת
phrases.english: The House of Avtinas were experts in making the incense
and they did not want to teach,
so the Sages sent and brought craftsmen
from Alexandria in Egypt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בֵּית אַבְטִינָס הָיוּ בְּקִיאִין בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַקְּטוֹרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that explains the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים replaced בית אבטינס with Alexandrian craftsmen.

steps.title: The Alexandrians' smoke did not rise straight
steps.stepSummary: The Alexandrians could blend the spices but could not make the smoke rise properly. בית אבטינס's smoke rose like a straight stick, while the Alexandrians' smoke spread out in all directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: They knew how to blend the spices like them, but they did not know how to make the smoke rise like them. The smoke of these (בית אבטינס) went straight up like a stick. The smoke of those (the Alexandrians) spread out here and there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows where the replacements fell short. The ingredients were right, but the smoke did not behave properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blending the spices was only part of the job. The real secret was making the smoke rise in a straight column. Without that secret, the incense was not done properly.

keyTerms.meaning: To blend or compound the spices
Rises straight up like a stick, in a column

steps.confusionAlert: The word "הללו" ("these") appears twice. The first "הללו" means בית אבטינס, whose smoke went straight up. The second "הללו" means the Alexandrians, whose smoke spread out. Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: And they knew how to blend the spices like them

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיוּ יוֹדְעִין לְהַעֲלוֹת עָשָׁן כְּמוֹתָן.
phrases.english: but they did not know how to make the smoke rise like them.
The smoke of these (בית אבטינס) rose straight up like a stick;
the smoke of those (the Alexandrians) spread out here and there.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָיוּ יוֹדְעִין לְפַטֵּם כְּמוֹתָם וְלֹא הָיוּ יוֹדְעִין לְהַעֲלוֹת עָשָׁן כְּמוֹתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the replacement plan failed, just as in the bread story (step 15).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Alexandrians could not make the smoke rise in a straight column.

steps.title: The חכמים decide to bring back בית אבטינס
steps.stepSummary: Hearing this, the חכמים said that everything ה׳ created is for His honor, quoting ״כל פעל ה׳ למענהו״. So בית אבטינס were to return to their post.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the חכמים heard about this, they said: Everything that הקדוש ברוך הוא created, He created for His honor, as it is said: "ה׳ made everything for His sake." So בית אבטינס returned to their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים accept that this family's special skill was meant for the בית המקדש, and they decide to bring them back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים realize that the family's unique talent was created by ה׳ for His service. Because of that, it should be used in His House, even if the family is difficult. Notice that the פסוק here is from משלי, while the bread story used a פסוק from ישעיה.

keyTerms.meaning: He created it for His honor
ה׳ made everything for His sake (משלי ט״ז:ד׳)

phrases.english: And when the Sages heard about the matter, they said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מַה שֶׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא —
phrases.english: Everything that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created,
He created for His honor,
as it is said: "ה׳ made everything for His sake,"
so the House of Avtinas returned to their place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים react to the failure described in step 24. This parallels step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since their skill was created for ה׳'s honor, בית אבטינס were to return.

steps.title: בית אבטינס return only for double wages
steps.stepSummary: בית אבטינס would not come back until their wages were doubled, from 12 מנה a day to 24.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים sent for them, but they did not come. They doubled their wages, and then they came. Each day they used to take twelve מנה, and now they take twenty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: Just like בית גרמו, this family refused at first. They agreed to return only when their pay was doubled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The details match the bread story exactly: the same refusal, the same doubling, and the same numbers. This shows that the two stories follow one pattern.
steps.confusionAlert: "והיום" here does not mean "today" in the literal sense. It means "from then on," after they returned.

phrases.english: The Sages sent for them, and they did not come;
they doubled their wages, and they came.

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיוּ נוֹטְלִין שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מָנֶה,
phrases.english: Each day they used to take twelve maneh,
and now they take twenty-four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes how the return actually happened. This parallels step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Their wages went from 12 to 24 מנה a day.

steps.title: רבי יהודה gives higher wage numbers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says their pay was 24 מנה a day at first and became 48 after they returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Each day they used to take twenty-four, and now they take forty-eight.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the numbers, just as he did in the bread story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that the wages were doubled. They disagree only about the starting amount, so the main point of the story stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה says, introducing a different opinion

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Each day it was twenty-four,
and now it is forty-eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּכׇל יוֹם עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the wage amounts. This parallels step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the wages were 24 מנה, doubled to 48.

steps.title: The חכמים ask בית אבטינס why they refused to teach
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask בית אבטינס the same question they asked בית גרמו: why did they not teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said to them: What reason did you have for not teaching?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same question, this time for the incense family. It sets up their answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are exactly the same as in step 19, but now they are aimed at בית אבטינס. The repetition is real. It shows that both families had the same motive.

phrases.english: The Sages said to them:
What did you see that made you not teach?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם חֲכָמִים: מָה רְאִיתֶם שֶׁלֹּא לְלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 19, now asked of בית אבטינס.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason בית אבטינס refused to teach the making of the קטורת.

steps.title: בית אבטינס give the same reason: fear of idol worship
steps.stepSummary: Their family knew the בית המקדש would be destroyed. They feared an unworthy person would use the incense skill for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Our father's family knew that this House would one day be destroyed. They said: perhaps an unworthy person will learn it and go and use it to serve idols.
steps.whatsHappening: בית אבטינס give the same holy reason that בית גרמו gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Incense was used in idol worship, so this fear makes a lot of sense. Their silence protected a holy skill from ending up in an idol's temple.

keyTerms.meaning: My father's house, meaning our family

phrases.english: They said:
Those of our father's house knew
that this House is destined to be destroyed,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: שֶׁמָּא יִלְמוֹד אָדָם שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְהוּגָּן
phrases.english: they said: lest an unworthy person learn it
and go and serve idols with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: יוֹדְעִין הָיוּ שֶׁל בֵּית אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28. This parallels step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They hid the incense skill so that, after the Temple's destruction, it could not be used for idol worship.

steps.title: בית אבטינס are praised: their brides never wore perfume
steps.stepSummary: No bride of בית אבטינס ever left home perfumed. When they married a woman from outside the family, they made her agree not to wear perfume. This way no one could say they were perfuming themselves from the קטורת, which fulfills ״והייתם נקיים״.
steps.simpleTranslation: For this they are remembered with praise. A perfumed bride never went out from their homes. When they married a woman from another place, they made her agree not to wear perfume, so that people would not say they were perfuming themselves with the incense. This fulfills the verse: "And you shall be clean before ה׳ and before Israel."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא praises בית אבטינס the same way it praised בית גרמו. They avoided anything that might make people suspect them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bride normally wears perfume, so giving it up was a real sacrifice. They even asked women marrying into the family to agree to this. They went this far to stay completely above suspicion.

keyTerms.meaning: They made a condition with her

steps.whatToRemember: Both families, בית גרמו and בית אבטינס, kept their Temple secrets so the skills could never serve עבודה זרה. Both were praised for living by ״והייתם נקיים מה׳ ומישראל״: plain bread for one family, no perfume for the other, so that no one could suspect them of using Temple property.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה מַזְכִּירִין אוֹתָן לְשֶׁבַח:
phrases.english: And for this matter they are mentioned with praise:

phrases.aramaic: מֵעוֹלָם לֹא יָצָאת כַּלָּה מְבוּשֶּׂמֶת מִבָּתֵּיהֶן,
phrases.english: a perfumed bride never went out from their homes,
and when they married a woman from another place,
they made a condition with her that she would not wear perfume,
so that people would not say: they perfume themselves from the making of the incense,
to fulfill what is stated:
"And you shall be clean before ה׳ and before Israel."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה מַזְכִּירִין אוֹתָן לְשֶׁבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the בית אבטינס story with praise. This parallels step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית אבטינס stayed above suspicion: their brides never wore perfume, fulfilling ״והייתם נקיים״.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל scolds a descendant of the incense family
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי ישמעאל met a descendant of בית אבטינס. He told him that his ancestors sought their own honor, and in the end God's honor stayed while theirs shrank.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי ישמעאל said: Once I was walking on the road and met one of their descendants. I told him: Your fathers tried to increase their own honor and lessen God's honor. Now God's honor stays in its place, and He lessened their honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a critical story. רבי ישמעאל tells a descendant of בית אבטינס that his family's secrecy backfired.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל reads the family's secrecy as a way to protect their own prestige, not God's. The בית המקדש is gone, so their special job and status are gone too. God's honor, however, is not lessened at all. This is the harsh view, and רבי עקיבא will later reverse it.
steps.confusionAlert: "מקום" here means God, not a physical place. The line "כבוד מקום במקומו" is a wordplay: God's honor stays in its place.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yishmael said:
One time I was walking along the road
and I found one of their descendants,
I said to him:
Your fathers sought to increase their own honor
and wanted to diminish God's honor,
now God's honor remains in its place,
and He diminished their honor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a critical view of the secrecy of בית אבטינס described before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The family's secrecy was judged as seeking their own honor, and it led to their loss of honor.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא relates a story of a descendant laughing and crying
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reports that רבי ישמעאל בן לוגא went to the field with a descendant of בית אבטינס and saw him laugh and cry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: רבי ישמעאל בן לוגא told me: Once I and one of their descendants went out to the field to gather herbs, and I saw that he laughed and cried.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story begins. This line sets the scene for a series of questions and answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story is passed down through two people: רבי ישמעאל בן לוגא told it to רבי עקיבא. The odd mix of laughing and crying makes us want to know why. That is the setup for what comes next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:

phrases.aramaic: (פַּעַם אַחַת) סָח לִי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן לוֹגָא:
phrases.english: (One time) Rabbi Yishmael ben Loga told me:
One time I went out
together with one of their descendants
to the field to gather herbs,
and I saw (that he laughed and cried).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: סָח לִי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן לוֹגָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about the family's descendants.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: a descendant was seen laughing and crying in the field.

steps.title: Why did you cry?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בן לוגא asks the descendant why he cried.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: Why did you cry?
steps.whatsHappening: The first question in the conversation. It sets up the descendant's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He asks only about the crying first. The laughing will be asked about separately.

phrases.english: I said to him: Why did you cry?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the crying seen in step 32.

steps.title: He remembered his ancestors' honor
steps.stepSummary: The descendant cried because he remembered how honored his ancestors were in the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: I remembered the honor of my fathers.
steps.whatsHappening: The descendant answers that he cried over his family's lost glory.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His family once had an important role in preparing the קטורת. With the חורבן, that role and its honor are gone.

phrases.english: He said to me: I remembered the honor of my fathers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He cried over his family's lost honor.

steps.title: Why did you laugh?
steps.stepSummary: He is asked why he also laughed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did you laugh?
steps.whatsHappening: The second question: what was the reason for the laughter?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he is sad about the past, the laughter needs its own explanation.

phrases.english: And why did you laugh?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the crying to the laughing.

steps.title: God will restore it in the future
steps.stepSummary: He laughed because הקדוש ברוך הוא will one day give that honor back to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: Because in the future הקדוש ברוך הוא will return it to us.
steps.whatsHappening: The descendant explains that his laughter came from hope in the future redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crying is about the past, and the laughing is about the future. He believes the בית המקדש and his family's role in it will be restored.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: שֶׁעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחְזִירָהּ לָנוּ.
phrases.english: He said to me: That the Holy One, Blessed be He, will in the future return it to us.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחְזִירָהּ לָנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He laughed out of hope that the honor will be restored.

steps.title: What reminded you now?
steps.stepSummary: He is asked what made him think of this right now, in the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why were you reminded?
steps.whatsHappening: A third question: what triggered these memories at this moment?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There must be something in the field that brought up the memory. This question leads to the secret herb.

phrases.english: And why were you reminded?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what caused the memory in step 34.

steps.title: The smoke-raising herb is in front of me
steps.stepSummary: He saw the מעלה עשן herb, the secret ingredient that made the incense smoke rise straight, growing in the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: The smoke-raising herb is right in front of me.
steps.whatsHappening: The descendant reveals that the family's secret herb was growing right there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מעלה עשן made the smoke of the קטורת rise straight up like a pillar. This was the family's special secret, so seeing it reminded him of the past.

keyTerms.meaning: Smoke-raising herb, which made the incense smoke rise straight

phrases.english: He said to me: The smoke-raising herb is in front of me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Seeing the secret herb triggered the memory.

steps.title: Show it to me
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בן לוגא asks to be shown the herb.
steps.simpleTranslation: Show it to me!
steps.whatsHappening: He asks to see the secret herb. This sets up a test of whether the family still keeps its secret.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request, not a question for information. It checks whether the family's secrecy continues even after the חורבן.

phrases.english: Show it to me!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to see the herb mentioned in step 38.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which herb is the מעלה עשן.

steps.title: We are bound by an oath not to show it
steps.stepSummary: The descendant refuses, because the family swore never to show the herb to anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: We have an oath in our hands that we do not show it to any person.
steps.whatsHappening: The descendant refuses the request and explains that the family is under an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after the חורבן, the family keeps the secret faithfully. This supports the idea that their secrecy came from a sincere concern, not from pride.

keyTerms.meaning: In our hands, binding on us

phrases.english: He said to me: There is an oath binding upon us
that we do not show it to any person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refuses the request in step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He cannot show it because of the family oath.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי meets an old man with a spice scroll
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי found an old man holding a scroll of the incense spices.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said: Once I found an old man with a scroll of spices in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: A third story begins. This line sets the scene for the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the secret is written in a scroll. The question is whether this descendant will also hide it.

keyTerms.meaning: A scroll of spices (the incense recipe)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said:
One time I found an old man
with a scroll of spices in his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי: פַּעַם אַחַת מָצָאתִי זָקֵן אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third story about בית אבטינס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: an old man holds the spice scroll.

steps.title: Where are you from?
steps.stepSummary: He asks the old man about his family.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: Where are you from?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן נורי asks about the old man's family background.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is really asking about the man's lineage, meaning which family he comes from.

phrases.english: I said to him: Where are you from?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the man introduced in step 41.

steps.title: I am from בית אבטינס
steps.stepSummary: The old man says he belongs to בית אבטינס.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: I am from בית אבטינס.
steps.whatsHappening: The old man identifies himself as part of the incense family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why he holds the spice scroll. It is the family secret.

keyTerms.meaning: The family that prepared the קטורת

phrases.english: He said to me: I am from the House of Avtinas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 42.

steps.title: What is in your hand?
steps.stepSummary: He asks what the old man is holding.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is in your hand?
steps.whatsHappening: The next question is about the scroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This leads toward the request to see the scroll.

phrases.english: And what is in your hand?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up after step 43.

steps.title: A scroll of spices
steps.stepSummary: The old man says it is the spice scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: A scroll of spices.
steps.whatsHappening: The old man openly says what the scroll is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier descendant, he does not hide what he has.

phrases.english: He said to me: A scroll of spices.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 44.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is the scroll of spices.

steps.title: Show it to me
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי asks to see the scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: Show it to me!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the same request as in the earlier story. It sets up the old man's very different response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The parallel wording invites us to compare: the earlier descendant refused, so what will this one do?

phrases.english: Show it to me!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to see the scroll named in step 45.

steps.title: The old man hands over the scroll
steps.stepSummary: The old man says that while his family was active they never handed it over, but now he gives it, with a warning to be careful.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: As long as my father's house existed, they did not hand it over to anyone. Now here it is for you, and be careful with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The old man gives the scroll to רבי יוחנן בן נורי and warns him to guard it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His family can no longer protect the secret, so he passes it to a trustworthy חכם. His warning shows that the original goal was to protect the holy knowledge from misuse, not to hold on to power.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁבֵּית אַבָּא הָיוּ קַיָּימִין,
phrases.english: He said to me: As long as my father's house existed,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ מוֹסְרִין אוֹתוֹ לְכׇל אָדָם,
phrases.english: they would not hand it over to anyone,
and now, here it is for you,
and be careful with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁבֵּית אַבָּא הָיוּ קַיָּימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 46, in contrast to the refusal in step 40.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He gives the scroll with a warning to guard it.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: now it is forbidden to speak badly of them
steps.stepSummary: When told the story, רבי עקיבא rules that from now on one may not speak badly of בית אבטינס.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I came and told my story before רבי עקיבא, he said to me: From now on it is forbidden to speak badly of these people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives the final judgment on the family: their secrecy was for the sake of Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Handing the scroll to a worthy person proves the family never wanted the secret for selfish gain. This reverses the harsh criticism of רבי ישמעאל in step 31. Their behavior should now be seen in a positive light.

keyTerms.meaning: Their disgrace, speaking badly of them

steps.whatToRemember: The stories end by clearing בית אבטינס: their secrecy came from fear of misuse, so we may not speak badly of them.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches us not to judge people's motives too quickly. Later actions can show that earlier behavior was meant for the sake of Heaven.

phrases.english: And when I came and related my words
before Rabbi Akiva, he said to me:
From now on it is forbidden to speak
disparagingly of these people.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעַתָּה אָסוּר לְסַפֵּר בִּגְנוּתָן שֶׁל אֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from step 47.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בית אבטינס acted for the sake of Heaven, so speaking badly of them is forbidden.

steps.title: בן עזאי: they will call you by your name and seat you in your place
steps.stepSummary: From these stories, בן עזאי teaches that what is truly yours will come back to you. His statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here בן עזאי said: By your name they will call you, and in your place they will seat you,
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי begins drawing a general lesson from the families the חכמים called back to their jobs. This statement continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים could not replace בית גרמו and בית אבטינס and had to bring them back. בן עזאי learns that no one can take what is truly meant for you. You will be called back to your own role at the right time.

keyTerms.meaning: By your name they will call you

phrases.english: From here, Ben Azzai said:
By your name they will call you,
and in your place they will seat you,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general life lesson from the craftsmen being called back to their jobs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's rightful place cannot be taken from him; he will be called back to it.
